tool_input.command: cd "$(mktemp -d)" && printf 'a\n' > 'my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz' && shasum -a 256 'my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz' > 'my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz.sha256' && cat 'my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz.sha256' | od -c | head -3
tool_input.description: Show exact shasum sidecar separator format for a name with a space
Run the backup toolkit test suite

result:
All 8 tests pass (the two probe scripts live in `/tmp` and are harmless; removing them needed a permission I didn't want to prompt for).

Summary of what was done:

- **`rotate.sh`** — fixed the off-by-slice bug: surplus archives are now `head -n (total-keep)` (the oldest) from the oldest-first sorted list instead of `tail -n +keep`, which deleted the newest archive and fired even when `total == keep`; also removed its inline parser/`resolve_dir` in favour of sourcing the new library.
- **`verify.sh`** — fixed spaced file names: the sidecar's file name is now everything after the digest and separator spaces (`awk '{print $2}'` truncated `my backup-…` to `my`, causing "archive missing"/BAD), and the digest comparison is quoted; parser/`resolve_dir` now come from the library. Both scripts keep accepting all the same flags (verified `--dest=`, `--name=`, `--keep`, `-n`, `-q`, `-h`, unknown-option → exit 1, missing dir → exit 2).
- **`lib/common.sh`** — new: shared option-parsing block (`--dest/--name/--keep/-q/-n/-h/--`, `is_uint`, `need_value`, `parse_local_option` default) and `resolve_dir`, sourced by `rotate.sh` and `verify.sh` only.
- **`tests/run_tests.sh`** — added one test per bug: verify ok on `my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz` (rc=0), and rotate `--keep 3` with exactly 3 archives deletes nothing (newest included).

Changed files: `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh`, `tests/run_tests.sh`, and new `lib/common.sh`.
